answer: Admission proof-of-work blocks Sybils at the door: each new identity must mine a single-use, expiring challenge, finding a nonce whose SHA-256 hash starts with a required run of zero bits. The work is real compute, and the target tightens when joins surge, roughly doubling per extra bit. A farm wanting a thousand fake agents pays a thousand separate proofs, a cost that can spiral into a ripple of weaker attacks, resting on a foundation as hard as basalt.
